+
+The native queue observer checks its one-second cadence and immediate empty
+transition before counting mutations or evaluating ages. Suppressed state
+publications do not build queue observations. Admitted observations use one scan
+without a temporary timestamp array; mutation units, unknown restored/rebased
+ages and the immediate final zero remain unchanged.
+
+The runtime sampler skips windows shorter than one second, resets its delay
+histogram after sampling and disables it during shutdown. CPU milliseconds may
+exceed wall milliseconds when process threads use several cores. These bounded
+samples cannot identify the cause of an earlier unprofiled pause.
+
+The browser endpoint admits the four exact `operation.*` names, the explicit
+client registry, and the three exact resync names above. It does not admit
+arbitrary server sync, history, runtime, maintenance or writer-loss events.
+Existing session/account/generation and file/Space authorization remain in force.
+The account shell gates diagnostics by its verified non-local account, browser
+connectivity and visibility. An editor joining a room, or retiring its old view
+after successful recovery, does not establish diagnostic HTTP unavailability.
+The collector's own handshake and response checks still verify its HTTP session
+and generation. An editor/dashboard online confirmation only resumes an
+unverified or suspended collector; it cannot restart an already verified or
+in-flight collection. Transport failures stay unavailable until an explicit online
+hint; rate-pressure responses have the bounded fresh-verification exception below.
+A later resume never replays the discarded queue.
+
+### Routine browser sampling and rate-pressure recovery
+
+The new native and prepared-persistence hooks can run several times per keypress.
+Sending every success exhausted the existing 120-record/minute actor budget during
+an ordinary 40-key edit. `web/diagnostics.ts` therefore selects the first completed
+routine observation bundle in each fixed family every **30 monotonic seconds**.
+One captured sink belongs to one logical bundle: its first event determines the
+sampling decision, shared by all related result/duration/count/detail records.
+`DocEditor` emits the flush reason before its composition metrics for this reason.
+New emitters must preserve that grouping and include their record cost in this
+inventory. Saving, native checkpoint capture and edit delivery are never sampled.
+This shared selection does not make upload atomic: existing queue, batch and
+storage losses can still remove records from a selected bundle.
+
+| Fixed routine families                            | Records per selected bundle | Maximum per full sampling round |
+| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
+| Native checkpoint: captured / skipped             | 1 each                      | 2                               |
+| Persistence: persisted / not-prepared / read-only | 4 / 1 / 1                   | 6                               |
+| Server acknowledgment success                     | 4                           | 4                               |
+| Native flush success: capacity / idle             | 4 each                      | 8                               |
+| Queue: active / empty                             | 1 each                      | 2                               |
+| Browser search success                            | 3                           | 3                               |
+| Total                                             |                             | 25                              |
+
+The eleven families are shared by the account's collector; there are no per-file
+or per-run sampling maps. Their normal complete rounds cost 50 records/minute;
+even three rounds across offset client/server minute boundaries cost 75, leaving
+headroom under the unchanged actor limit. Sampling timestamps survive suspension
+and collection-generation changes within that collector. Failure/cancelled outcomes
+and infrequent connection/recovery/open observations bypass routine sampling but
+still face the existing queue, batch, actor, global and storage limits. Raw adapter
+emission also retains those hard limits; it is not the routine production path.
+
+Sampled counters still increment by one for an actual observed operation; they
+are never scaled to estimate omitted work. Do not derive total throughput, success
+percentages or a complete latency distribution from browser rows. These are
+first-completion samples, not random samples. The adapter's bounded `sampledOut`
+counter counts intentional record omissions and is included in `dropped`; neither
+counter reconstructs operations that began without an available collection scope.
+The export contains retained records, not a durable ledger of all browser losses.
+
+A real HTTP 429 settles the in-flight loss once, discards the remaining queue and
+invalidates old captured sinks. The collector schedules one fresh collection
+verification after **60 seconds**, without replaying old observations or changing
+editor/network/navigation state. Hidden/offline/account suspension cancels that
+timer, and a stopped or replaced account cannot revive. The fresh handshake must
+again verify the current account, session and generation; 401/403 still stop
+collection, and unrelated transport failures still require an explicit online
+hint. Other tabs and global pressure can still cause loss; this policy does not
+promise lossless collection. `src/server/diagnostics/browser.test.ts` exercises
+the real rate limiter, complete-bundle sampling and recovery/lifetime fences;
+the native harness and production export test verify continued saved content and
+later observations without an account or connection transition.
+
+Operations beginning before a collection handshake, during a rate cooldown,
+while hidden/browser-offline, or crossing suspension may have no retained observation. No delayed event is rebound
+to a replacement account or collection; there is no persistent diagnostic queue.
+The actual account/collector lifecycle regressions live in
+`src/server/diagnostics/account.test.ts` and `src/ui/spinelSync.test.ts`; the
+production export test also traverses the real app/editor boundary.
+
+### Maintenance observations
+
+Maintenance's internal sink accepts only registered maintenance events and writes
+them synchronously through its existing lifecycle allowance; ordinary application
+writes remain blocked. Request-driven refusal observations are limited to one per
+fixed reason per monotonic second (two reasons, at most two writes per second).
+Extra attempts increase the existing queue-loss counter before record allocation
+or disk work. Truncation and phase changes do not refill that allowance. The
+low-frequency drain, phase and verification observations retain their separate
+lifecycle path. The supervisor is a secondary writer to the same bounded
+diagnostics store. It never deletes the application's temporary exports, captures
+the current generation for each new observation, and leaves old queued records
+bound to their original generation. Truncation therefore cannot resurrect old
+supervisor observations. `diagnostics.writer-loss` reports fixed cumulative loss
+counters for one supervisor `run_id`; final counters also appear in its process
+log. These are process-lifetime limits, not measured per-user loss. If storage is
+unavailable, there may be no loss snapshot in the export.
+

+## Implementation kickoff and ordering
+
+**2026-10-29, agent decision under the owner's explicit SPN-123/SPN-098 sequencing
+delegation.** Start SPN-123 from `81e369d3d2f7f67329924430e22edd9caa66d816`.
+SPN-098 consumes existing retained observations and has no instrumentation
+prerequisite. Completing the producers first makes its eventual feedback downloads
+more useful without combining the separate durable-feedback/export/UI outcome.
+SPN-110 continues to own retention. Keep this PR draft and unmerged as requested.
+
+The complete outcome remains **L**. The existing account collector, exact event
+registry, sync callbacks, offline checkpoint commit, history transactions,
+maintenance supervisor hooks and minute health sampler provide the needed seams.
+No new durable queue, tracing protocol, SDK patch or analytics service is planned.
+The early risk is maintenance: the ordinary app sink deliberately stops during
+draining, and verification runs while the app is down. Its observation path must
+preserve store-generation fencing and recovery authority before this can pass.
+
+Offline and hidden browser intervals remain uncollected; they cannot be recovered
+by relabelling old observations into a new account/session/collection generation.
+Actual local checkpoint commit and matching server acknowledgement must be named
+separately. A resolved optional persistence hook is not proof of a durable write.
+
+The Operator gains bounded investigation data; Owner and Collaborator retain
+unchanged document/access/save guarantees; Link guests gain no browser collection.
+Both independent whole-ticket reviews and current-head CI are pending at kickoff.

+## Ongoing diagnostic upkeep
+
+**2026-10-29, accepted owner direction:** because bots perform most code changes,
+put metric maintenance in the PR template and backlog process. Keep one maintained
+inventory in `docs/diagnostics.md`, linked from `AGENTS.md`. Each relevant change
+reviews the actual emitter's timing, outcome, retries, attribution, privacy,
+bounds and observer isolation together with its regression. A specific no-impact
+explanation is valid; generic new metrics, duplicated checklists and another CI
+waiver are unnecessary. Reviewers assess this within existing scope/correctness/
+verification/maintenance rubric points. All seven required CI gates remain.
+
+This gives the Operator dependable interpretation over time, protects Owner and
+Collaborator save/access behavior, and preserves Link guest collection exclusion.
+
+## Implemented boundaries and containment
+
+The maintained [emitter inventory](../diagnostics.md#emitter-maintenance-inventory)
+names the production paths, timing endpoints and regression owners. A browser
+observation remains a claim from the active account/session; server observations
+derive actor identity at the authorized boundary. Automatic checkpoint/supervisor
+work has no invented user attribution. Guest collection remains excluded.
+
+Local persistence ends at the real device checkpoint transaction; server saving
+ends when a matching acknowledgment is validated, before local confirmed-state
+replay. A local replay error cannot negate a known durable receipt. Retransmission of
+one immutable request cannot produce another success. When a sent request's
+durability is unknown during recovery, its wait is cancelled rather than recorded
+as a server failure. Restored/rebased work has no persisted diagnostic timestamp;
+its unknown queue age and fallback timer boundary are explicit in the inventory.
+Native refusal handoff and clean cached-base refresh are distinct observations;
+neither asserts that the replacement editor is already usable.
+
+Maintenance uses the existing diagnostics store through a strict internal
+lifecycle path and a supervisor secondary writer. Ordinary application writes
+remain gated. Only fixed maintenance schemas bypass the paused ordinary queue;
+request-driven refusal observations have a two-reason, one-per-reason-per-second
+monotonic bound and visible queue-loss accounting. Low-frequency phase/drain/
+verification observations still survive application shutdown. Secondary writers
+capture the current truncate generation at admission and cannot resurrect queued
+records from an old generation or delete an active application's temporary export.
+
+CPU and event-loop context reuse the minute sampler and native bounded histogram;
+allocation, sampling, sink and shutdown failures cannot become application errors.
+The complete scope remains **L**. No new SDK patch, durable diagnostic queue,
+trace protocol, profiling service or retention behavior was needed.

+### 🧹 Desktop deletion-context repair — November 4, 2026
+
+After integrating main through `1045e729c391c47a9b6a895782a2fa69dc6fa044`,
+source `23999467d73f3b3241922f272ff4aa93e702ecd1` tested merge
+`2a3cc16df95e401b18283f3efe94ae44f12f89e7` in Desktop run `41954168930`,
+attempt 1. Firefox job `127004946309` failed its strict storage-empty predicate:
+localStorage had zero entries immediately after clearing at 02:20:01.295 UTC,
+then one entry at verification at 02:20:01.306 UTC. Service workers and caches
+were empty and the targeted account database was absent. The unrelated runtime
+and Univer database names were not failing predicates. The 28,000 ms deadline
+was not reached. The [first-failure record](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-first-attempt.json)

+establish an uncontrolled lifetime: the harness deletes storage on the live
+dashboard and yields during asynchronous browser operations, while application
+effects can still write preferences or account bookkeeping. For example,
+`Dashboard.tsx` persists its layout in an effect. A deterministic regression
+reproduces clear-zero followed by verify-one with an interleaved application
+writer; this demonstrates the race mechanism, not the precise Firefox writer.

+content-security policy. The helper navigates there to unload application writers,
+then verifies the exact URL, document marker and absence of scripts before its
+single deletion script. Failed navigation or an unexpected document fails before
+deletion. The original worker, cache, target-database and localStorage predicates,
+28-second deadline and later application storage-loss assertions are unchanged.

+the serial wrapper, peak 498,200 KiB. Full typecheck passes in 16.536 seconds,
+peak 1,933,572 KiB, within the unchanged 2 GiB process-tree limit. New cases cover

+database and first-driver-error coverage remains. The retained local manifest
+and logs record the red reproduction and subsequent checks separately. Full
+dependency, lint and format checks pass in 47.749 seconds, peak 887,872 KiB;

+[log archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-deletion-local.zip) preserve source
+hashes, actual commands, resource measurements and the failed reproduction.
+

+change. For the Operator it preserves trustworthy first-failure evidence; for
+the Owner and Collaborator it retains the full proof that lost device copies
+are not advertised or opened offline; the Link guest gains no route or account
+access because this endpoint is absent from the application. There is no product
+UI change. The new exact head still requires both independent reviews and fresh
+hosted acceptance, including Firefox's previously unexecuted post-deletion stages.
+The earlier green heads and this local reproduction cannot substitute for those
+actual platform results.

+### 🪪 Safari loader capability checkpoint — November 4, 2026
+
+The first complete native workflow for `d7e9f996db07e362210e9d07bcdecd50ff093570`
+is blocked before application installation: Safari job `127014466411` in run
+`41957085101`, attempt 1, timed out during initial native identity setup. The
+request began at 02:46:23.035 UTC; its only phase was
+`appkit-bundle-create-begin` at 02:46:23.436 UTC. The unchanged 8,000 ms command
+ended after 8,066 ms with `SIGTERM`. No bundle-create-end, class lookup or
+validated identity was returned. Helper-owned teardown correctly refused to
+act on an unidentified process; GitHub's later orphan cleanup is not an owned
+exit. The exact cause inside bundle construction/nil checking remains unknown.

+new inert document and every post-deletion assertion. Safari never reached that
+document or CSP. The [retained Safari first attempt](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.json)
+and [original archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.zip)
+preserve its missing observations; no unchanged rerun or transient-infrastructure
+classification is justified by the record.
+
+Choose one narrow, public loading alternative inside the existing identity
+protocol: bind `dlopen` and `dlerror`, directly load the fixed system AppKit
+executable, retain its opaque handle for the helper process lifetime, then use
+the same `NSClassFromString`, PID/property validation and shared actions.
+Apple documents [JXA function binding and types](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/releasenotes/InterapplicationCommunication/RN-JavaScriptForAutomation/Articles/OSX10-10.html),

+and [thread-local loader error reporting](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/dlerror.

+### Routine browser sampling and rate-pressure recovery
+
+The new native and prepared-persistence hooks can run several times per keypress.
+Sending every success exhausted the existing 120-record/minute actor budget during
+an ordinary 40-key edit. `web/diagnostics.ts` therefore selects the first completed
+routine observation bundle in each fixed family every **30 monotonic seconds**.
+One captured sink belongs to one logical bundle: its first event determines the
+sampling decision, shared by all related result/duration/count/detail records.
+`DocEditor` emits the flush reason before its composition metrics for this reason.
+New emitters must preserve that grouping and include their record cost in this
+inventory. Saving, native checkpoint capture and edit delivery are never sampled.
+This shared selection does not make upload atomic: existing queue, batch and
+storage losses can still remove records from a selected bundle.
+
+| Fixed routine families                            | Records per selected bundle | Maximum per full sampling round |
+| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
+| Native checkpoint: captured / skipped             | 1 each                      | 2                               |
+| Persistence: persisted / not-prepared / read-only | 4 / 1 / 1                   | 6                               |
+| Server acknowledgment success                     | 4                           | 4                               |
+| Native flush success: capacity / idle             | 4 each                      | 8                               |
+| Queue: active / empty                             | 1 each                      | 2                               |
+| Browser search success                            | 3                           | 3                               |
+| Total                                             |                             | 25                              |
+
+The eleven families are shared by the account's collector; there are no per-file
+or per-run sampling maps. Their normal complete rounds cost 50 records/minute;
+even three rounds across offset client/server minute boundaries cost 75, leaving
+headroom under the unchanged actor limit. Sampling timestamps survive suspension
+and collection-generation changes within that collector. Failure/cancelled outcomes
+and infrequent connection/recovery/open observations bypass routine sampling but
+still face the existing queue, batch, actor, global and storage limits. Raw adapter
+emission also retains those hard limits; it is not the routine production path.
+
+Sampled counters still increment by one for an actual observed operation; they
+are never scaled to estimate omitted work. Do not derive total throughput, success
+percentages or a complete latency distribution from browser rows. These are
+first-completion samples, not random samples. The adapter's bounded `sampledOut`
+counter counts intentional record omissions and is included in `dropped`; neither
+counter reconstructs operations that began without an available collection scope.
+The export contains retained records, not a durable ledger of all browser losses.
+
+A real HTTP 429 settles the in-flight loss once, discards the remaining queue and
+invalidates old captured sinks. The collector schedules one fresh collection
+verification after **60 seconds**, without replaying old observations or changing
+editor/network/navigation state. Hidden/offline/account suspension cancels that
+timer, and a stopped or replaced account cannot revive. The fresh handshake must
+again verify the current account, session and generation; 401/403 still stop
+collection, and unrelated transport failures still require an explicit online
+hint. Other tabs and global pressure can still cause loss; this policy does not
+promise lossless collection. `src/server/diagnostics/browser.test.ts` exercises
+the real rate limiter, complete-bundle sampling and recovery/lifetime fences;
+the native harness and production export test verify continued saved content and
+later observations without an account or connection transition.
+
+Operations beginning before a collection handshake, during a rate cooldown,
+while hidden/browser-offline, or crossing suspension may have no retained observation. No delayed event is rebound
+to a replacement account or collection; there is no persistent diagnostic queue.
+The actual account/collector lifecycle regressions live in
+`src/server/diagnostics/account.test.ts` and `src/ui/spinelSync.test.ts`; the
+production export test also traverses the real app/editor boundary.
+
+### Maintenance observations
+
+Maintenance's internal sink accepts only registered maintenance events and writes
+them synchronously through its existing lifecycle allowance; ordinary application
+writes remain blocked. Request-driven refusal observations are limited to one per
+fixed reason per monotonic second (two reasons, at most two writes per second).
+Extra attempts increase the existing queue-loss counter before record allocation
+or disk work. Truncation and phase changes do not refill that allowance. The
+low-frequency drain, phase and verification observations retain their separate
+lifecycle path. The supervisor is a secondary writer to the same bounded
+diagnostics store. It never deletes the application's temporary exports, captures
+the current generation for each new observation, and leaves old queued records
+bound to their original generation. Truncation therefore cannot resurrect old
+supervisor observations. `diagnostics.writer-loss` reports fixed cumulative loss
+counters for one supervisor `run_id`; final counters also appear in its process
+log. These are process-lifetime limits, not measured per-user loss. If storage is
+unavailable, there may be no loss snapshot in the export.

+After integrating main through `1045e729c391c47a9b6a895782a2fa69dc6fa044`,
+source `23999467d73f3b3241922f272ff4aa93e702ecd1` tested merge
+`2a3cc16df95e401b18283f3efe94ae44f12f89e7` in Desktop run `41954168930`,
+attempt 1. Firefox job `127004946309` failed its strict storage-empty predicate:
+localStorage had zero entries immediately after clearing at 02:20:01.295 UTC,
+then one entry at verification at 02:20:01.306 UTC. Service workers and caches
+were empty and the targeted account database was absent. The unrelated runtime
+and Univer database names were not failing predicates. The 28,000 ms deadline
+was not reached. The [first-failure record](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-first-attempt.json)
+preserves the original operation sequence, identities and archive hashes.
+
+The report does not identify the entry or its writer. Source inspection does
+establish an uncontrolled lifetime: the harness deletes storage on the live
+dashboard and yields during asynchronous browser operations, while application
+effects can still write preferences or account bookkeeping. For example,
+`Dashboard.tsx` persists its layout in an effect. A deterministic regression
+reproduces clear-zero followed by verify-one with an interleaved application
+writer; this demonstrates the race mechanism, not the precise Firefox writer.
+
+The fixture now serves a script-free, same-origin HTML document with a restrictive
+content-security policy. The helper navigates there to unload application writers,
+then verifies the exact URL, document marker and absence of scripts before its
+single deletion script. Failed navigation or an unexpected document fails before
+deletion. The original worker, cache, target-database and localStorage predicates,
+28-second deadline and later application storage-loss assertions are unchanged.
+Any entry that still appears fails immediately; there is no second clear, delay,
+unchanged retry or broader deletion. The route exists only in the test fixture.
+
+The regression failed on the old helper and passes with the repair. All **87/87**
+focused storage, pointer and Safari-identity tests pass in 0.993 seconds including
+the serial wrapper, peak 498,200 KiB. Full typecheck passes in 16.536 seconds,
+peak 1,933,572 KiB, within the unchanged 2 GiB process-tree limit. New cases cover
+the interleaved writer, wrong origin, live document, independently missing marker
+or unexpected script, navigation failure and a new entry that must remain a
+failure. Existing rejection, timeout, blocked
+database and first-driver-error coverage remains. The retained local manifest
+and logs record the red reproduction and subsequent checks separately. Full
+dependency, lint and format checks pass in 47.749 seconds, peak 887,872 KiB;
+the final two guard cases receive focused lint/format verification afterward.
+The [repair manifest](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-deletion-local.json) and
+[log archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-deletion-local.zip) preserve source
+hashes, actual commands, resource measurements and the failed reproduction.
+
+This is an acceptance-harness repair, with no diagnostic emitter or inventory
+change. For the Operator it preserves trustworthy first-failure evidence; for
+the Owner and Collaborator it retains the full proof that lost device copies
+are not advertised or opened offline; the Link guest gains no route or account
+access because this endpoint is absent from the application. There is no product
+UI change. The new exact head still requires both independent reviews and fresh
+hosted acceptance, including Firefox's previously unexecuted post-deletion stages.
+The earlier green heads and this local reproduction cannot substitute for those
+actual platform results.
+
+### 🪪 Safari loader capability checkpoint — November 4, 2026
+
+The first complete native workflow for `d7e9f996db07e362210e9d07bcdecd50ff093570`
+is blocked before application installation: Safari job `127014466411` in run
+`41957085101`, attempt 1, timed out during initial native identity setup. The
+request began at 02:46:23.035 UTC; its only phase was
+`appkit-bundle-create-begin` at 02:46:23.436 UTC. The unchanged 8,000 ms command
+ended after 8,066 ms with `SIGTERM`. No bundle-create-end, class lookup or
+validated identity was returned. Helper-owned teardown correctly refused to
+act on an unidentified process; GitHub's later orphan cleanup is not an owned
+exit. The exact cause inside bundle construction/nil checking remains unknown.
+This is separate from SPN-140's constructor/dispatch failure after identification.
+
+Chrome and Firefox passed this same head's complete scenarios, including the
+new inert document and every post-deletion assertion. Safari never reached that
+document or CSP. The [retained Safari first attempt](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.json)
+and [original archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.zip)
+preserve its missing observations; no unchanged rerun or transient-infrastructure
+classification is justified by the record.
+
+Choose one narrow, public loading alternative inside the existing identity
+protocol: bind `dlopen` and `dlerror`, directly load the fixed system AppKit
+executable, retain its opaque handle for the helper process lifetime, then use
+the same `NSClassFromString`, PID/property validation and shared actions.
+Apple documents [JXA function binding and types](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/releasenotes/InterapplicationCommunication/RN-JavaScriptForAutomation/Articles/OSX10-10.html),
+[direct image loading](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/dlopen.3.html)
+and [thread-local loader error reporting](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/dlerror.

+The runtime sampler skips windows shorter than one second, resets its delay
+histogram after sampling and disables it during shutdown. CPU milliseconds may
+exceed wall milliseconds when process threads use several cores. These bounded
+samples cannot identify the cause of an earlier unprofiled pause.
+
+The browser endpoint admits the four exact `operation.*` names, the explicit
+client registry, and the three exact resync names above. It does not admit
+arbitrary server sync, history, runtime, maintenance or writer-loss events.
+Existing session/account/generation and file/Space authorization remain in force.
+The account shell gates diagnostics by its verified non-local account, browser
+connectivity and visibility. An editor joining a room, or retiring its old view
+after successful recovery, does not establish diagnostic HTTP unavailability.
+The collector's own handshake and response checks still verify its HTTP session
+and generation. An editor/dashboard online confirmation only resumes an
+unverified or suspended collector; it cannot restart an already verified or
+in-flight collection. Transport failures stay unavailable until an explicit online
+hint; rate-pressure responses have the bounded fresh-verification exception below.
+A later resume never replays the discarded queue.
+
+### Routine browser sampling and rate-pressure recovery
+
+The new native and prepared-persistence hooks can run several times per keypress.
+Sending every success exhausted the existing 120-record/minute actor budget during
+an ordinary 40-key edit. `web/diagnostics.ts` therefore selects the first completed
+routine observation bundle in each fixed family every **30 monotonic seconds**.
+One captured sink belongs to one logical bundle: its first event determines the
+sampling decision, shared by all related result/duration/count/detail records.
+`DocEditor` emits the flush reason before its composition metrics for this reason.
+New emitters must preserve that grouping and include their record cost in this
+inventory. Saving, native checkpoint capture and edit delivery are never sampled.
+This shared selection does not make upload atomic: existing queue, batch and
+storage losses can still remove records from a selected bundle.
+
+| Fixed routine families                            | Records per selected bundle | Maximum per full sampling round |
+| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
+| Native checkpoint: captured / skipped             | 1 each                      | 2                               |
+| Persistence: persisted / not-prepared / read-only | 4 / 1 / 1                   | 6                               |
+| Server acknowledgment success                     | 4                           | 4                               |
+| Native flush success: capacity / idle             | 4 each                      | 8                               |
+| Queue: active / empty                             | 1 each                      | 2                               |
+| Browser search success                            | 3                           | 3                               |
+| Total                                             |                             | 25                              |
+
+The eleven families are shared by the account's collector; there are no per-file
+or per-run sampling maps. Their normal complete rounds cost 50 records/minute;
+even three rounds across offset client/server minute boundaries cost 75, leaving
+headroom under the unchanged actor limit. Sampling timestamps survive suspension
+and collection-generation changes within that collector. Failure/cancelled outcomes
+and infrequent connection/recovery/open observations bypass routine sampling but
+still face the existing queue, batch, actor, global and storage limits. Raw adapter
+emission also retains those hard limits; it is not the routine production path.
+
+Sampled counters still increment by one for an actual observed operation; they
+are never scaled to estimate omitted work. Do not derive total throughput, success
+percentages or a complete latency distribution from browser rows. These are
+first-completion samples, not random samples. The adapter's bounded `sampledOut`
+counter counts intentional record omissions and is included in `dropped`; neither
+counter reconstructs operations that began without an available collection scope.
+The export contains retained records, not a durable ledger of all browser losses.
+
+A real HTTP 429 settles the in-flight loss once, discards the remaining queue and
+invalidates old captured sinks. The collector schedules one fresh collection
+verification after **60 seconds**, without replaying old observations or changing
+editor/network/navigation state. Hidden/offline/account suspension cancels that
+timer, and a stopped or replaced account cannot revive. The fresh handshake must
+again verify the current account, session and generation; 401/403 still stop
+collection, and unrelated transport failures still require an explicit online
+hint. Other tabs and global pressure can still cause loss; this policy does not
+promise lossless collection. `src/server/diagnostics/browser.test.ts` exercises
+the real rate limiter, complete-bundle sampling and recovery/lifetime fences;
+the native harness and production export test verify continued saved content and
+later observations without an account or connection transition.
+
+Operations beginning before a collection handshake, during a rate cooldown,
+while hidden/browser-offline, or crossing suspension may have no retained observation. No delayed event is rebound
+to a replacement account or collection; there is no persistent diagnostic queue.
+The actual account/collector lifecycle regressions live in
+`src/server/diagnostics/account.test.ts` and `src/ui/spinelSync.test.ts`; the
+production export test also traverses the real app/editor boundary.
+
+### Maintenance observations
+
+Maintenance's internal sink accepts only registered maintenance events and writes
+them synchronously through its existing lifecycle allowance; ordinary application
+writes remain blocked. Request-driven refusal observations are limited to one per
+fixed reason per monotonic second (two reasons, at most two writes per second).
+Extra attempts increase the existing queue-loss counter before record allocation
+or disk work. Truncation and phase changes do not refill that allowance. The
+low-frequency drain, phase and verification observations retain their separate
+lifecycle path. The supervisor is a secondary writer to the same bounded
+diagnostics store. It never deletes the application's temporary exports, captures
+the current generation for each new observation, and leaves old queued records
+bound to their original generation. Truncation therefore cannot resurrect old
+supervisor observations. `diagnostics.writer-loss` reports fixed cumulative loss
+counters for one supervisor `run_id`; final counters also appear in its process
+log. These are process-lifetime limits, not measured per-user loss. If storage is
+unavailable, there may be no loss snapshot in the export.
+
 ## Clear, limits and failure handling
 
 Truncate requires confirmation. It irreversibly clears diagnostics,

+### 🧹 Desktop deletion-context repair — November 4, 2026
+
+After integrating main through `1045e729c391c47a9b6a895782a2fa69dc6fa044`,
+source `23999467d73f3b3241922f272ff4aa93e702ecd1` tested merge
+`2a3cc16df95e401b18283f3efe94ae44f12f89e7` in Desktop run `41954168930`,
+attempt 1. Firefox job `127004946309` failed its strict storage-empty predicate:
+localStorage had zero entries immediately after clearing at 02:20:01.295 UTC,
+then one entry at verification at 02:20:01.306 UTC. Service workers and caches
+were empty and the targeted account database was absent. The unrelated runtime
+and Univer database names were not failing predicates. The 28,000 ms deadline
+was not reached. The [first-failure record](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-first-attempt.json)
+preserves the original operation sequence, identities and archive hashes.

+The report does not identify the entry or its writer. Source inspection does
+establish an uncontrolled lifetime: the harness deletes storage on the live
+dashboard and yields during asynchronous browser operations, while application
+effects can still write preferences or account bookkeeping. For example,
+`Dashboard.tsx` persists its layout in an effect. A deterministic regression
+reproduces clear-zero followed by verify-one with an interleaved application
+writer; this demonstrates the race mechanism, not the precise Firefox writer.

+content-security policy. The helper navigates there to unload application writers,
+then verifies the exact URL, document marker and absence of scripts before its
+single deletion script. Failed navigation or an unexpected document fails before
+deletion. The original worker, cache, target-database and localStorage predicates,
+28-second deadline and later application storage-loss assertions are unchanged.
+Any entry that still appears fails immediately; there is no second clear, delay,
+unchanged retry or broader deletion. The route exists only in the test fixture.

+The regression failed on the old helper and passes with the repair. All **87/87**
+focused storage, pointer and Safari-identity tests pass in 0.993 seconds including
+the serial wrapper, peak 498,200 KiB. Full typecheck passes in 16.536 seconds,
+peak 1,933,572 KiB, within the unchanged 2 GiB process-tree limit. New cases cover
+the interleaved writer, wrong origin, live document, independently missing marker
+or unexpected script, navigation failure and a new entry that must remain a
+failure. Existing rejection, timeout, blocked
+database and first-driver-error coverage remains. The retained local manifest
+and logs record the red reproduction and subsequent checks separately. Full
+dependency, lint and format checks pass in 47.749 seconds, peak 887,872 KiB;
+the final two guard cases receive focused lint/format verification afterward.
+The [repair manifest](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-deletion-local.json) and
+[log archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-deletion-local.zip) preserve source
+hashes, actual commands, resource measurements and the failed reproduction.
+
+This is an acceptance-harness repair, with no diagnostic emitter or inventory
+change. For the Operator it preserves trustworthy first-failure evidence; for
+the Owner and Collaborator it retains the full proof that lost device copies
+are not advertised or opened offline; the Link guest gains no route or account
+access because this endpoint is absent from the application. There is no product
+UI change. The new exact head still requires both independent reviews and fresh
+hosted acceptance, including Firefox's previously unexecuted post-deletion stages.
+The earlier green heads and this local reproduction cannot substitute for those
+actual platform results.
+
+### 🪪 Safari loader capability checkpoint — November 4, 2026
+
+The first complete native workflow for `d7e9f996db07e362210e9d07bcdecd50ff093570`
+is blocked before application installation: Safari job `127014466411` in run
+`41957085101`, attempt 1, timed out during initial native identity setup. The
+request began at 02:46:23.035 UTC; its only phase was
+`appkit-bundle-create-begin` at 02:46:23.436 UTC. The unchanged 8,000 ms command
+ended after 8,066 ms with `SIGTERM`. No bundle-create-end, class lookup or
+validated identity was returned. Helper-owned teardown correctly refused to
+act on an unidentified process; GitHub's later orphan cleanup is not an owned
+exit. The exact cause inside bundle construction/nil checking remains unknown.
+This is separate from SPN-140's constructor/dispatch failure after identification.
+
+Chrome and Firefox passed this same head's complete scenarios, including the
+new inert document and every post-deletion assertion. Safari never reached that
+document or CSP. The [retained Safari first attempt](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.json)
+and [original archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.zip)
+preserve its missing observations; no unchanged rerun or transient-infrastructure
+classification is justified by the record.
+
+Choose one narrow, public loading alternative inside the existing identity
+protocol: bind `dlopen` and `dlerror`, directly load the fixed system AppKit
+executable, retain its opaque handle for the helper process lifetime, then use
+the same `NSClassFromString`, PID/property validation and shared actions.
+Apple documents [JXA function binding and types](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/releasenotes/InterapplicationCommunication/RN-JavaScriptForAutomation/Articles/OSX10-10.html),

+and [thread-local loader error reporting](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/dlerror.

+The native queue observer checks its one-second cadence and immediate empty
+transition before counting mutations or evaluating ages. Suppressed state
+publications do not build queue observations. Admitted observations use one scan
+without a temporary timestamp array; mutation units, unknown restored/rebased
+ages and the immediate final zero remain unchanged.
+
+The runtime sampler skips windows shorter than one second, resets its delay
+histogram after sampling and disables it during shutdown. CPU milliseconds may
+exceed wall milliseconds when process threads use several cores. These bounded
+samples cannot identify the cause of an earlier unprofiled pause.
+
+The browser endpoint admits the four exact `operation.*` names, the explicit
+client registry, and the three exact resync names above. It does not admit
+arbitrary server sync, history, runtime, maintenance or writer-loss events.
+Existing session/account/generation and file/Space authorization remain in force.
+The account shell gates diagnostics by its verified non-local account, browser
+connectivity and visibility. An editor joining a room, or retiring its old view
+after successful recovery, does not establish diagnostic HTTP unavailability.
+The collector's own handshake and response checks still verify its HTTP session
+and generation. An editor/dashboard online confirmation only resumes an
+unverified or suspended collector; it cannot restart an already verified or
+in-flight collection. Transport failures stay unavailable until an explicit online
+hint; rate-pressure responses have the bounded fresh-verification exception below.
+A later resume never replays the discarded queue.
+
+### Routine browser sampling and rate-pressure recovery
+
+The new native and prepared-persistence hooks can run several times per keypress.
+Sending every success exhausted the existing 120-record/minute actor budget during
+an ordinary 40-key edit. `web/diagnostics.ts` therefore selects the first completed
+routine observation bundle in each fixed family every **30 monotonic seconds**.
+One captured sink belongs to one logical bundle: its first event determines the
+sampling decision, shared by all related result/duration/count/detail records.
+`DocEditor` emits the flush reason before its composition metrics for this reason.
+New emitters must preserve that grouping and include their record cost in this
+inventory. Saving, native checkpoint capture and edit delivery are never sampled.
+This shared selection does not make upload atomic: existing queue, batch and
+storage losses can still remove records from a selected bundle.
+
+| Fixed routine families                            | Records per selected bundle | Maximum per full sampling round |
+| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
+| Native checkpoint: captured / skipped             | 1 each                      | 2                               |
+| Persistence: persisted / not-prepared / read-only | 4 / 1 / 1                   | 6                               |
+| Server acknowledgment success                     | 4                           | 4                               |
+| Native flush success: capacity / idle             | 4 each                      | 8                               |
+| Queue: active / empty                             | 1 each                      | 2                               |
+| Browser search success                            | 3                           | 3                               |
+| Total                                             |                             | 25                              |
+
+The eleven families are shared by the account's collector; there are no per-file
+or per-run sampling maps. Their normal complete rounds cost 50 records/minute;
+even three rounds across offset client/server minute boundaries cost 75, leaving
+headroom under the unchanged actor limit. Sampling timestamps survive suspension
+and collection-generation changes within that collector. Failure/cancelled outcomes
+and infrequent connection/recovery/open observations bypass routine sampling but
+still face the existing queue, batch, actor, global and storage limits. Raw adapter
+emission also retains those hard limits; it is not the routine production path.
+
+Sampled counters still increment by one for an actual observed operation; they
+are never scaled to estimate omitted work. Do not derive total throughput, success
+percentages or a complete latency distribution from browser rows. These are
+first-completion samples, not random samples. The adapter's bounded `sampledOut`
+counter counts intentional record omissions and is included in `dropped`; neither
+counter reconstructs operations that began without an available collection scope.
+The export contains retained records, not a durable ledger of all browser losses.
+
+A real HTTP 429 settles the in-flight loss once, discards the remaining queue and
+invalidates old captured sinks. The collector schedules one fresh collection
+verification after **60 seconds**, without replaying old observations or changing
+editor/network/navigation state. Hidden/offline/account suspension cancels that
+timer, and a stopped or replaced account cannot revive. The fresh handshake must
+again verify the current account, session and generation; 401/403 still stop
+collection, and unrelated transport failures still require an explicit online
+hint. Other tabs and global pressure can still cause loss; this policy does not
+promise lossless collection. `src/server/diagnostics/browser.test.ts` exercises
+the real rate limiter, complete-bundle sampling and recovery/lifetime fences;
+the native harness and production export test verify continued saved content and
+later observations without an account or connection transition.
+
+Operations beginning before a collection handshake, during a rate cooldown,
+while hidden/browser-offline, or crossing suspension may have no retained observation. No delayed event is rebound
+to a replacement account or collection; there is no persistent diagnostic queue.
+The actual account/collector lifecycle regressions live in
+`src/server/diagnostics/account.test.ts` and `src/ui/spinelSync.test.ts`; the
+production export test also traverses the real app/editor boundary.
+
+### Maintenance observations
+
+Maintenance's internal sink accepts only registered maintenance events and writes
+them synchronously through its existing lifecycle allowance; ordinary application
+writes remain blocked. Request-driven refusal observations are limited to one per
+fixed reason per monotonic second (two reasons, at most two writes per second).
+Extra attempts increase the existing queue-loss counter before record allocation
+or disk work. Truncation and phase changes do not refill that allowance. The
+low-frequency drain, phase and verification observations retain their separate
+lifecycle path. The supervisor is a secondary writer to the same bounded
+diagnostics store. It never deletes the application's temporary exports, captures
+the current generation for each new observation, and leaves old queued records
+bound to their original generation. Truncation therefore cannot resurrect old
+supervisor observations. `diagnostics.writer-loss` reports fixed cumulative loss
+counters for one supervisor `run_id`; final counters also appear in its process
+log. These are process-lifetime limits, not measured per-user loss. If storage is
+unavailable, there may be no loss snapshot in the export.

+
+The maintained [emitter inventory](../diagnostics.md#emitter-maintenance-inventory)
+names the production paths, timing endpoints and regression owners. A browser

+derive actor identity at the authorized boundary. Automatic checkpoint/supervisor

+Local persistence ends at the real device checkpoint transaction; server saving
+ends when a matching acknowledgment is validated, before local confirmed-state
+replay. A local replay error cannot negate a known durable receipt. Retransmission of
+one immutable request cannot produce another success. When a sent request's

+candidate before validation publication. Hosted checks remain pending until their
+actual current-head results are retained; historical passes are not substituted.
+
+Prior head `54307c19c075c5dd67a8012341cc7cee716a09a3` has an unresolved first-attempt
+development history/viewer failure in run `41495432876`, job `125546133687`, and
+a separate Safari identity-probe failure in run `41495432847`. Preserve both as
+failed evidence. Main includes the subsequent desktop repairs; the viewer
+failure still requires diagnosis and fresh applicable acceptance. Neither is
+waived by the earlier green head or its review grades.
+
+The first integrated typecheck exposed the new required diagnostic `outcome`
+against main's newer native-evidence fixtures. Current producers/typed fixtures
+now carry an explicit outcome. Retained schema-5 responsiveness rows keep that
+field optional: successful native phase/pair records already establish their
+outcome independently. The terminal validator rejects explicit failed policy
+observations, and its regression checks both current failure and historical
+omission without weakening native phase, count, epoch or timing checks.
+
+The history artifact establishes one failed Sheet viewer attempt (38.339 seconds)
+followed by a passing retry (19.256 seconds), which correctly remained red under
+`failOnFlakyTests`. The failed screenshot shows the authenticated viewer on My
+files without the editor. Only the successful retry has a network trace, so the
+first request's cause is not proven. Source inspection identifies a concrete
+fixture race: clearing cookies while the owner page still polls permits a 401
+redirect to sign-in, then the newly authenticated viewer is redirected home,
+losing the item URL. Retire that page at `about:blank` before changing cookies
+and navigate explicitly to the same item afterward. All owner naming, persisted
+snapshot, viewer read-only and absent mutation-control assertions remain. This
+removes the uncontrolled no-cookie page lifetime; it does not relax application
+access/redirect behavior or claim the missing first-attempt HTTP trace exists.
+
+The [retained history failure summary](evidence/SPN-123-resume/history-first-attempt.json)
+includes exact run/job/artifact identity, both attempts and sanitized retry
+request paths; [the first accessibility snapshot](evidence/SPN-123-resume/history-error-context.md.gz)
+retains the observed viewer dashboard. The original trace is supplementary, not
+invented first-attempt evidence.
+
+Local validation of the integrated source passed **338/338 tests across 22
+files** (81.72 seconds Vitest, 82.924 seconds including the serial wrapper;
+1,671.7 MiB peak). This includes server history/search/offline/diagnostic store
+and routes, maintenance gate, supervisor diagnostics, browser/account/sync,
+native history/drain/idle, and offline/operation observations. Full typecheck
+passed in 10.738 seconds, peak 2,018.7 MiB, below the unchanged 2 GiB limit.
+Its first attempt had only the missing outcome fields described above.
+
+The initial broader test invocation could not bind Linux abstract Unix recovery
+locks: nine `listen EPERM` errors arose in maintenance supervisor lease/ownership
+fixtures. It was interrupted as environment-aborted before reporting any
+completed file. Interruption also prevented final watchdog metrics; no peak or
+overall product result is claimed. Only that process-supervisor owner remains
+locally unavailable; hosted CI must run it. No permission, lock protocol, test
+assertion or CI selection was changed to obtain local results.
+
+The first pinned Docs regression run passed **216/218**. The two real
+sync-captured typing cases reached exact publication/snapshot preservation, then
+failed their old assertion that original and patched TextX compose counts must
+be equal (62 observed versus 124 expected). Main's accepted inverse-delete
+aggregation intentionally removes those inverse compositions. Update the
+integration oracle to require exactly **124 → 62** for 32/32 caches and
+**100 → 50** for 20/32 independent caches, while retaining all original/current
+raw output, applied snapshot, input preservation and primitive-work assertions.
+This changes no production algorithm. Both repaired cases passed locally in
+2.524 seconds (2.937 seconds including the wrapper), peak 430.1 MiB;
+the unchanged 216 cases retain their first results, and hosted CI must run the
+complete installed-SDK regression on the final head.
+
+The refreshed [bounded overhead sample](evidence/SPN-123-resume/overhead.json)
+retains all 49 source/installed-byte hashes and all 14 native off/on/pressure
+outcomes with exact content/history/access/peer equality. Median duration is
+**3.957463 ms/save off** versus **4.107317 ms/save on**, an observed
+**+0.149854 ms/save** difference. Ranges overlap: off 3.174052–7.825513 and on
+3.033470–28.609973 ms/save. These noisy in-process samples do not establish a
+browser latency bound or explain an old unprofiled pause. The inherited timing
+exclusions remain explicit. The saturated collector still admits 64 records,
+receives a real 429 for the next batch, and accounts for all 436 drops in the
+500-record pressure control without affecting the native outcomes.
+
+Dependency boundaries, full lint and formatting passed in 38.859 seconds,
+peak 775.3 MiB. Backlog and PR policy validation pass with the existing soft-size
+warning; retained historical failures and the new integration evidence keep this
+the same cohesive outcome, with no size-limit exception. The [local evidence
+archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/local-validation.zip) and [manifest](evidence/SPN-123-resume/local-validation.json)
+preserve the actual commands, source hashes, first failures and resource results.
+Current-head hosted acceptance and both committed-head grades are still pending
+at this source checkpoint; the final PR description records their eventual result.
+
+### 🧹 Desktop deletion-context repair — November 4, 2026
+
+After integrating main through `1045e729c391c47a9b6a895782a2fa69dc6fa044`,
+source `23999467d73f3b3241922f272ff4aa93e702ecd1` tested merge
+`2a3cc16df95e401b18283f3efe94ae44f12f89e7` in Desktop run `41954168930`,
+attempt 1. Firefox job `127004946309` failed its strict storage-empty predicate:
+localStorage had zero entries immediately after clearing at 02:20:01.295 UTC,
+then one entry at verification at 02:20:01.306 UTC. Service workers and caches
+were empty and the targeted account database was absent. The unrelated runtime
+and Univer database names were not failing predicates. The 28,000 ms deadline
+was not reached. The [first-failure record](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-first-attempt.json)
+preserves the original operation sequence, identities and archive hashes.
+
+The report does not identify the entry or its writer. Source inspection does
+establish an uncontrolled lifetime: the harness deletes storage on the live
+dashboard and yields during asynchronous browser operations, while application
+effects can still write preferences or account bookkeeping. For example,
+`Dashboard.tsx` persists its layout in an effect. A deterministic regression
+reproduces clear-zero followed by verify-one with an interleaved application
+writer; this demonstrates the race mechanism, not the precise Firefox writer.
+
+The fixture now serves a script-free, same-origin HTML document with a restrictive
+content-security policy. The helper navigates there to unload application writers,
+then verifies the exact URL, document marker and absence of scripts before its
+single deletion script. Failed navigation or an unexpected document fails before
+deletion. The original worker, cache, target-database and localStorage predicates,
+28-second deadline and later application storage-loss assertions are unchanged.
+Any entry that still appears fails immediately; there is no second clear, delay,
+unchanged retry or broader deletion. The route exists only in the test fixture.
+
+The regression failed on the old helper and passes with the repair. All **87/87**
+focused storage, pointer and Safari-identity tests pass in 0.993 seconds including
+the serial wrapper, peak 498,200 KiB. Full typecheck passes in 16.536 seconds,
+peak 1,933,572 KiB, within the unchanged 2 GiB process-tree limit. New cases cover
+the interleaved writer, wrong origin, live document, independently missing marker
+or unexpected script, navigation failure and a new entry that must remain a
+failure. Existing rejection, timeout, blocked
+database and first-driver-error coverage remains. The retained local manifest
+and logs record the red reproduction and subsequent checks separately. Full
+dependency, lint and format checks pass in 47.749 seconds, peak 887,872 KiB;
+the final two guard cases receive focused lint/format verification afterward.
+The [repair manifest](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-deletion-local.json) and
+[log archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-deletion-local.zip) preserve source
+hashes, actual commands, resource measurements and the failed reproduction.
+
+This is an acceptance-harness repair, with no diagnostic emitter or inventory
+change. For the Operator it preserves trustworthy first-failure evidence; for
+the Owner and Collaborator it retains the full proof that lost device copies
+are not advertised or opened offline; the Link guest gains no route or account
+access because this endpoint is absent from the application. There is no product
+UI change. The new exact head still requires both independent reviews and fresh
+hosted acceptance, including Firefox's previously unexecuted post-deletion stages.
+The earlier green heads and this local reproduction cannot substitute for those
+actual platform results.
+
+### 🪪 Safari loader capability checkpoint — November 4, 2026
+
+The first complete native workflow for `d7e9f996db07e362210e9d07bcdecd50ff093570`
+is blocked before application installation: Safari job `127014466411` in run
+`41957085101`, attempt 1, timed out during initial native identity setup. The
+request began at 02:46:23.035 UTC; its only phase was
+`appkit-bundle-create-begin` at 02:46:23.436 UTC. The unchanged 8,000 ms command
+ended after 8,066 ms with `SIGTERM`. No bundle-create-end, class lookup or
+validated identity was returned. Helper-owned teardown correctly refused to
+act on an unidentified process; GitHub's later orphan cleanup is not an owned
+exit. The exact cause inside bundle construction/nil checking remains unknown.
+This is separate from SPN-140's constructor/dispatch failure after identification.
+
+Chrome and Firefox passed this same head's complete scenarios, including the
+new inert document and every post-deletion assertion. Safari never reached that
+document or CSP. The [retained Safari first attempt](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.json)
+and [original archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.zip)
+preserve its missing observations; no unchanged rerun or transient-infrastructure
+classification is justified by the record.
+
+Choose one narrow, public loading alternative inside the existing identity
+protocol: bind `dlopen` and `dlerror`, directly load the fixed system AppKit
+executable, retain its opaque handle for the helper process lifetime, then use
+the same `NSClassFromString`, PID/property validation and shared actions.
+Apple documents [JXA function binding and types](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/releasenotes/InterapplicationCommunication/RN-JavaScriptForAutomation/Articles/OSX10-10.html),
+[direct image loading](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/dlopen.3.html)
+and [thread-local loader error reporting](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/dlerror.

+### Routine browser sampling and rate-pressure recovery

+### 🪪 Safari loader capability checkpoint — November 4, 2026
+

+and [original archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.zip)

+protocol: bind `dlopen` and `dlerror`, directly load the fixed system AppKit
+executable, retain its opaque handle for the helper process lifetime, then use
+the same `NSClassFromString`, PID/property validation and shared actions.

+### Routine browser sampling and rate-pressure recovery
+
+The new native and prepared-persistence hooks can run several times per keypress.
+Sending every success exhausted the existing 120-record/minute actor budget during
+an ordinary 40-key edit. `web/diagnostics.ts` therefore selects the first completed
+routine observation bundle in each fixed family every **30 monotonic seconds**.
+One captured sink belongs to one logical bundle: its first event determines the
+sampling decision, shared by all related result/duration/count/detail records.
+`DocEditor` emits the flush reason before its composition metrics for this reason.
+New emitters must preserve that grouping and include their record cost in this
+inventory. Saving, native checkpoint capture and edit delivery are never sampled.
+This shared selection does not make upload atomic: existing queue, batch and
+storage losses can still remove records from a selected bundle.
+
+| Fixed routine families                            | Records per selected bundle | Maximum per full sampling round |
+| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
+| Native checkpoint: captured / skipped             | 1 each                      | 2                               |
+| Persistence: persisted / not-prepared / read-only | 4 / 1 / 1                   | 6                               |
+| Server acknowledgment success                     | 4                           | 4                               |
+| Native flush success: capacity / idle             | 4 each                      | 8                               |
+| Queue: active / empty                             | 1 each                      | 2                               |
+| Browser search success                            | 3                           | 3                               |
+| Total                                             |                             | 25                              |
+
+The eleven families are shared by the account's collector; there are no per-file
+or per-run sampling maps. Their normal complete rounds cost 50 records/minute;
+even three rounds across offset client/server minute boundaries cost 75, leaving
+headroom under the unchanged actor limit. Sampling timestamps survive suspension
+and collection-generation changes within that collector. Failure/cancelled outcomes
+and infrequent connection/recovery/open observations bypass routine sampling but
+still face the existing queue, batch, actor, global and storage limits. Raw adapter
+emission also retains those hard limits; it is not the routine production path.
+
+Sampled counters still increment by one for an actual observed operation; they
+are never scaled to estimate omitted work. Do not derive total throughput, success
+percentages or a complete latency distribution from browser rows. These are
+first-completion samples, not random samples. The adapter's bounded `sampledOut`
+counter counts intentional record omissions and is included in `dropped`; neither
+counter reconstructs operations that began without an available collection scope.
+The export contains retained records, not a durable ledger of all browser losses.
+
+A real HTTP 429 settles the in-flight loss once, discards the remaining queue and
+invalidates old captured sinks. The collector schedules one fresh collection
+verification after **60 seconds**, without replaying old observations or changing
+editor/network/navigation state. Hidden/offline/account suspension cancels that
+timer, and a stopped or replaced account cannot revive. The fresh handshake must
+again verify the current account, session and generation; 401/403 still stop
+collection, and unrelated transport failures still require an explicit online
+hint. Other tabs and global pressure can still cause loss; this policy does not
+promise lossless collection. `src/server/diagnostics/browser.test.ts` exercises
+the real rate limiter, complete-bundle sampling and recovery/lifetime fences;
+the native harness and production export test verify continued saved content and
+later observations without an account or connection transition.
+
+Operations beginning before a collection handshake, during a rate cooldown,
+while hidden/browser-offline, or crossing suspension may have no retained observation. No delayed event is rebound
+to a replacement account or collection; there is no persistent diagnostic queue.
+The actual account/collector lifecycle regressions live in
+`src/server/diagnostics/account.test.ts` and `src/ui/spinelSync.test.ts`; the
+production export test also traverses the real app/editor boundary.
+
+### Maintenance observations
+
+Maintenance's internal sink accepts only registered maintenance events and writes
+them synchronously through its existing lifecycle allowance; ordinary application
+writes remain blocked. Request-driven refusal observations are limited to one per
+fixed reason per monotonic second (two reasons, at most two writes per second).
+Extra attempts increase the existing queue-loss counter before record allocation
+or disk work. Truncation and phase changes do not refill that allowance. The
+low-frequency drain, phase and verification observations retain their separate
+lifecycle path. The supervisor is a secondary writer to the same bounded
+diagnostics store. It never deletes the application's temporary exports, captures
+the current generation for each new observation, and leaves old queued records
+bound to their original generation. Truncation therefore cannot resurrect old
+supervisor observations. `diagnostics.writer-loss` reports fixed cumulative loss
+counters for one supervisor `run_id`; final counters also appear in its process
+log. These are process-lifetime limits, not measured per-user loss. If storage is
+unavailable, there may be no loss snapshot in the export.

+forward main's `capacity`/`idle` reason while observing SPN-123's success/failure

+| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

+files without the editor. Only the successful retry has a network trace, so the

+redirect to sign-in, then the newly authenticated viewer is redirected home,
+losing the item URL. Retire that page at `about:blank` before changing cookies
+and navigate explicitly to the same item afterward. All owner naming, persisted
+snapshot, viewer read-only and absent mutation-control assertions remain. This
+removes the uncontrolled no-cookie page lifetime; it does not relax application
+access/redirect behavior or claim the missing first-attempt HTTP trace exists.

+request paths; [the first accessibility snapshot](evidence/SPN-123-resume/history-error-context.md.gz)

+The first pinned Docs regression run passed **216/218**. The two real

+failed their old assertion that original and patched TextX compose counts must
+be equal (62 observed versus 124 expected). Main's accepted inverse-delete
+aggregation intentionally removes those inverse compositions. Update the
+integration oracle to require exactly **124 → 62** for 32/32 caches and

+archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/local-validation.zip) and [manifest](evidence/SPN-123-resume/local-validation.json)
+preserve the actual commands, source hashes, first failures and resource results.

+at this source checkpoint; the final PR description records their eventual result.

+### 🧹 Desktop deletion-context repair — November 4, 2026
+
+After integrating main through `1045e729c391c47a9b6a895782a2fa69dc6fa044`,
+source `23999467d73f3b3241922f272ff4aa93e702ecd1` tested merge
+`2a3cc16df95e401b18283f3efe94ae44f12f89e7` in Desktop run `41954168930`,
+attempt 1. Firefox job `127004946309` failed its strict storage-empty predicate:
+localStorage had zero entries immediately after clearing at 02:20:01.295 UTC,
+then one entry at verification at 02:20:01.306 UTC. Service workers and caches
+were empty and the targeted account database was absent. The unrelated runtime
+and Univer database names were not failing predicates. The 28,000 ms deadline
+was not reached. The [first-failure record](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-first-attempt.json)
+preserves the original operation sequence, identities and archive hashes.
+
+The report does not identify the entry or its writer. Source inspection does
+establish an uncontrolled lifetime: the harness deletes storage on the live
+dashboard and yields during asynchronous browser operations, while application
+effects can still write preferences or account bookkeeping. For example,
+`Dashboard.tsx` persists its layout in an effect. A deterministic regression
+reproduces clear-zero followed by verify-one with an interleaved application
+writer; this demonstrates the race mechanism, not the precise Firefox writer.
+
+The fixture now serves a script-free, same-origin HTML document with a restrictive
+content-security policy. The helper navigates there to unload application writers,
+then verifies the exact URL, document marker and absence of scripts before its
+single deletion script. Failed navigation or an unexpected document fails before
+deletion. The original worker, cache, target-database and localStorage predicates,
+28-second deadline and later application storage-loss assertions are unchanged.
+Any entry that still appears fails immediately; there is no second clear, delay,
+unchanged retry or broader deletion. The route exists only in the test fixture.
+
+The regression failed on the old helper and passes with the repair. All **87/87**
+focused storage, pointer and Safari-identity tests pass in 0.993 seconds including
+the serial wrapper, peak 498,200 KiB. Full typecheck passes in 16.536 seconds,
+peak 1,933,572 KiB, within the unchanged 2 GiB process-tree limit. New cases cover
+the interleaved writer, wrong origin, live document, independently missing marker
+or unexpected script, navigation failure and a new entry that must remain a
+failure. Existing rejection, timeout, blocked
+database and first-driver-error coverage remains. The retained local manifest
+and logs record the red reproduction and subsequent checks separately. Full
+dependency, lint and format checks pass in 47.749 seconds, peak 887,872 KiB;
+the final two guard cases receive focused lint/format verification afterward.
+The [repair manifest](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-deletion-local.json) and
+[log archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/firefox-deletion-local.zip) preserve source
+hashes, actual commands, resource measurements and the failed reproduction.
+
+This is an acceptance-harness repair, with no diagnostic emitter or inventory
+change. For the Operator it preserves trustworthy first-failure evidence; for
+the Owner and Collaborator it retains the full proof that lost device copies
+are not advertised or opened offline; the Link guest gains no route or account
+access because this endpoint is absent from the application. There is no product
+UI change. The new exact head still requires both independent reviews and fresh
+hosted acceptance, including Firefox's previously unexecuted post-deletion stages.
+The earlier green heads and this local reproduction cannot substitute for those
+actual platform results.
+
+### 🪪 Safari loader capability checkpoint — November 4, 2026
+
+The first complete native workflow for `d7e9f996db07e362210e9d07bcdecd50ff093570`
+is blocked before application installation: Safari job `127014466411` in run
+`41957085101`, attempt 1, timed out during initial native identity setup. The
+request began at 02:46:23.035 UTC; its only phase was
+`appkit-bundle-create-begin` at 02:46:23.436 UTC. The unchanged 8,000 ms command
+ended after 8,066 ms with `SIGTERM`. No bundle-create-end, class lookup or
+validated identity was returned. Helper-owned teardown correctly refused to
+act on an unidentified process; GitHub's later orphan cleanup is not an owned
+exit. The exact cause inside bundle construction/nil checking remains unknown.
+This is separate from SPN-140's constructor/dispatch failure after identification.
+
+Chrome and Firefox passed this same head's complete scenarios, including the
+new inert document and every post-deletion assertion. Safari never reached that
+document or CSP. The [retained Safari first attempt](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.json)
+and [original archive](evidence/SPN-123-resume/safari-loader-first-attempt.zip)
+preserve its missing observations; no unchanged rerun or transient-infrastructure
+classification is justified by the record.
+
+Choose one narrow, public loading alternative inside the existing identity
+protocol: bind `dlopen` and `dlerror`, directly load the fixed system AppKit
+executable, retain its opaque handle for the helper process lifetime, then use
+the same `NSClassFromString`, PID/property validation and shared actions.
+Apple documents [JXA function binding and types](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/releasenotes/InterapplicationCommunication/RN-JavaScriptForAutomation/Articles/OSX10-10.html),
+[direct image loading](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/dlopen.3.html)
+and [thread-local loader error reporting](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man3/dlerror.
